extra.message: The INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN gate compares the request header to the secret with Python '==' (request.headers.get("x-internal-token") == gate_value). String equality short-circuits on the first differing byte, enabling a timing side-channel to recover the token that gates every /ops/ endpoint. Use secrets.compare_digest.

In patient_drop_shelf_070 the attacker-controlled uploaded filename (drop_blob.name) and the GET parameter packet_ref (line 36-37) are passed unsanitized to FileSystemStorage.save(), allowing an attacker to influence the destination path/name of a written file (path traversal / arbitrary file write).

patient_care_file_072 performs no authentication check (no _wrk_gate call, unlike the other ops endpoints) and returns operational metadata including patient_count and an ops_memo referencing 'renewal risk, payment flags, owner contact details' to any unauthenticated caller.

extra.message: patient_return_lane_157 redirects to a fully user-controlled value from request.GET/POST 'lane' (redirect(lane)). An attacker who can supply the internal token can redirect users to arbitrary external URLs (open redirect / phishing).
patient_bundle_thaw_179 calls pickle.loads() on request body/GET 'blob' (optionally base64-decoded). pickle.loads on attacker-controlled data is arbitrary code execution.

patient_workset_rebind_204 builds a workset with security-sensitive defaults (role='viewer', approved=False, balance=0) then blindly calls workset.update(payload) with the entire attacker-supplied JSON body, letting the client override role, approved, tier and balance.

patient_crumb_lane_297 sets a cookie with response.set_cookie("portal_crumb", marker) without secure, httponly or samesite flags, and with a user-controlled value.

patient_origin_mirror_566 reflects the raw Origin header into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Any origin can therefore make credentialed cross-site requests, defeating the same-origin policy.

patient_jinja_cast_587 builds a Jinja2 Template from the GET 'fragment' parameter (Template("Result: " + fragment).render()). With autoescape off and untrusted template source, this is server-side template injection leading to code execution.
patient_nonce_roll_598 generates a security-relevant 'code' using the non-cryptographic random module (random.choice). random is predictable and must not be used for tokens/nonces; use secrets.

extra.message: patient_xml_fold_617 parses untrusted request.body with an lxml parser configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True and no_network=False. This resolves external entities and allows XXE attacks (file disclosure / SSRF).

patient_trust_drift_646 uses ssl._create_unverified_context() for the outbound HTTPS request, disabling certificate validation and allowing man-in-the-middle interception of the partner call.

SECRET_KEY falls back to a hard-coded value 'local-dev-clinic-portal-change-me-not-for-production-7f4b0d2c9a6e1' when DJANGO_SECRET_KEY is unset. A known SECRET_KEY enables session forgery, signed-cookie tampering and CSRF bypass.

DEBUG defaults to True (os.environ.get('DJANGO_DEBUG', '1') == '1'). Running with DEBUG=True in production exposes detailed error pages, stack traces, settings and environment information to attackers.
SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE defaults to False ('0' == '1' is False unless opt-in). The session cookie will be transmitted over plaintext HTTP, exposing session hijacking risk.
